title: The Art of the Listing Pitch: Why Storytelling Wins in a Competitive Market
summary: REMAX agents share how preparation, storytelling and trust help turn listing appointments into lasting client relationships.
body_markdown:
Winning a listing often starts long before a real estate agent sits down with a homeowner. While market knowledge and pricing expertise are essential, top-performing agents know that earning a seller’s confidence requires more than presenting data. The strongest listing presentations combine research, strategy and communication to create a compelling narrative that helps sellers understand both their options and the value their agent brings to the table.


For[Kate Sweeten](https://www.remax.com/usa/en/residential/agent/chapin/kate-sweeten-100058084) , a Diamond Club Team Leader of The Sweeten Group with REMAX At the Lake in Chapin, South Carolina, success starts by avoiding assumptions.


Early in her career, Sweeten would arrive at listing appointments with extensive research and a price already in mind. Over time, she realized that no amount of online research could fully tell a home’s story.


“I am not there to force their home into a predetermined formula,” Sweeten says. “I am there to understand it first.”


Today, she focuses on learning about the property, the seller’s goals, and the property’s unique characteristics before developing a pricing and marketing strategy. Once she has seen the home and heard directly from the seller, she analyzes the data and builds recommendations tailored to their situation.


That personalized approach reflects an important lesson for agents: Winning a listing begins long before an agent presents their value proposition.


[Alex Irish](https://www.remax.ca/on/alex-irish-p100069590-ag) , a Pinnacle Club Team Leader of Regan Irish & Associates with REMAX Escarpment Realty Inc. in Oakville, Ontario, Canada, follows a similar philosophy. While she conducts extensive research before every appointment, including ownership records, sales history, market data and marketing plans, she avoids creating a predetermined pitch.


“I like to go into the appointment open minded and nimble, so I can customize the approach once I determine the clients’ needs and pain points,” Irish says.


[Brianna Castillo](https://www.remax.com/usa/en/residential/agent/dallas/brianna-castillo-100087992) , a Diamond Club Team Leader of Haven Realty Group with REMAX DFW Associates in Dallas, Texas, also views preparation as a critical differentiator. For Castillo, the listing appointment is simply the culmination of the work that has already happened behind the scenes.


“The appointment is where you apply the work you already did. It is not where the work happens,” Castillo says.


Castillo researches comparable sales, active competition and pricing risks before meeting a seller, often preparing recommendations well before a listing agreement is signed. She believes preparation gives agents the confidence to answer difficult questions and demonstrate their expertise. ****


**Turning Data Into a Story**


A strong listing presentation helps sellers understand what the data means and how it connects to a clear strategy. Sweeten believes data builds credibility, but storytelling brings those insights to life.


“I don’t want to hand someone 20 pages of comparable sales without explaining the story they tell,” she says.


Rather than focusing solely on statistics, she shows sellers why certain homes attracted buyers, why others struggled and how those lessons apply to their property. She also shares real examples from her own business to help clients understand the strategy behind her recommendations.


Irish takes a similar approach, using market data to support the narrative rather than drive the conversation.


“Initially it’s all about storytelling, building relationships and trust,” Irish says. “Data should be used only to support the story you’re selling.”


Castillo similarly views data, strategy and storytelling as complementary tools that each serve a different purpose during a presentation.


“Data answers, ‘Is this true?’ Strategy answers, ‘What does this mean for me specifically?’ Narrative answers, ‘Have you actually done this before?'” Castillo says.


She often uses real client experiences to help sellers understand how recommendations translate into outcomes, believing stories help build credibility in a way that facts can’t.


**Building Confidence Through Trust**


While every listing appointment is different, all three agents agree that trust is often the deciding factor.


For Sweeten, that means listening before presenting.


“Agents can become so focused on delivering their presentation that they never learn what the seller actually needs,” she says.


Irish focuses on understanding a client’s concerns, goals and expectations, so she can develop a pitch that feels personal and relevant. She emphasizes honesty throughout the process, even when market realities may not align with what a seller hopes to hear.


Castillo believes building trust starts with curiosity rather than an immediate strategy.


“First, ask enough questions to actually understand what type of listing and clients you’re dealing with,” Castillo says.


She encourages agents to uncover a seller’s motivations, concerns and previous experiences before discussing recommendations. According to Castillo, those conversations often reveal exactly what the client needs to hear in order to move forward confidently.


The agents also highlighted the importance of the first 24 hours before and after a listing appointment. Prompt communication, thoughtful follow-ups and executing on commitments help demonstrate what the client experience will be like moving forward.


Castillo describes that period as one of the most important opportunities to reinforce trust.


“Silence creates doubt. Speed creates confidence,” Castillo says.


Through proactive communication, clear timelines and active listening, she believes agents can demonstrate the level of service that sellers can expect throughout the transaction.


**A Repeatable Formula for Winning Listings**


While every agent has a unique style, the fundamentals of a successful listing presentation remain consistent. Preparation establishes credibility. Storytelling brings strategy to life. Trust creates confidence.


For agents looking to strengthen their own listing presentations, the advice from Sweeten, Irish and Castillo is clear: Do the work before the appointment, listen more than you talk and use data to support a story that is tailored to the seller’s goals. As many top agents have learned, winning listings isn’t about delivering a perfect pitch. It’s about earning a seller’s confidence through preparation, authentic storytelling and a client-first approach.


“Preparation gets you in the room. Performance wins the signature. Process builds the business,” Castillo says.
